problems.title: Formatting one line inside a multiline literal changes its value
problems.summary: A format range can put a marker inside a triple-quoted string or command. Indentation then changes inside the literal, including on repeated runs.

commits.title: Expand format ranges to cover whole multiline literals

fix.why_together: The release backport includes the formatter change and regression tests. The master-based topic commit adds the same source and test lines on that base.

validation.detail: 11,964 assertions passed and 16 pre-existing assertions were marked broken. All 47 --lines checks passed. Tested dogfood commit 3efa0c13d1a3b33b7686d97b27b6ed3d017f674a.

draft.title: Formatting one line inside a multiline literal changes its value
draft.body:
Save this file as `literal.jl` using the indentation shown.

```julia
begin
    s = """
    a
    b
    c
    """
end
```

Run `runic --lines=4:4 --diff literal.jl` with unpatched Runic 1.11.1. Only the line containing `b` gains indentation. Applying the edit changes the value of `s`, and formatting the same line again shifts it further. The expected diff for this file is empty.

Expand a selected range to the boundaries of any enclosing multiline string or command before inserting formatting markers. This keeps markers outside literal contents. Upstream issue #260 tracks the behavior.
